purpose: Specify a proposed synthetic sensor batch ingestion design with interfaces, failure handling, observability, rollout, and unresolved choices.

facts.text: The synthetic North Basin sensor fleet has 120 simulated devices that produce one reading per minute.
Definition: Each reading has a device ID, sequence number, capture timestamp, temperature value, and checksum.
Definition: The simulated sender may retry a batch after an ambiguous response, so duplicate submissions are expected.
The current exercise receiver stores readings in a single process memory map and loses them on restart.
Definition: The design goal is to preserve acknowledged readings across a receiver restart in the pilot.
Proposed: A proposed HTTPS endpoint accepts at most 100 readings per request and rejects larger requests before parsing individual readings.
Proposed: A proposed request size limit is 256 KiB of decoded body bytes.
Proposed: A proposed authentication port receives a trusted device principal from the host application; the payload device ID alone grants no authority.
Proposed: The proposed parser validates required fields, timestamp syntax, numeric temperature bounds of minus 40 to 125 Celsius, and checksum before persistence.
Proposed: The proposed duplicate key is the pair of trusted device principal and sequence number.
Proposed: A matching duplicate payload would return the prior receipt without writing a second reading.

Proposed: A duplicate key with different canonical reading content would return a conflict diagnostic and require investigation; the canonical encoding rules remain a versioned implementation decision.
Proposed: The proposed durable store is a local append-only segment log with a checksum per record and an fsync before success acknowledgment.
Proposed: The receiver would replay valid complete records after restart and stop at the first corrupt or partial tail record.

Proposed: A successful persistence receipt includes batch ID, accepted count, and store position, with no raw readings. A whole-batch rejection has a separate diagnostic with invalid item indexes and never claims accepted readings or a successful store position.
Proposed: A request may have valid and invalid readings; the proposed behavior is whole-batch rejection to avoid ambiguous partial retry semantics.
Proposed: The proposed response classes are 200 for exact duplicate receipt, 202 for newly persisted batch, 400 for malformed content, 409 for key conflict, and 503 for uncertain storage outcome.
Definition: A 503 response must not assert that the batch was absent because the write may have completed before the response failed.
Proposed: The proposed caller recovery is to retry with the same batch ID and device sequence numbers after 503.
Definition: The host application, not the ingestion library, owns TLS termination and principal authentication.
Proposed: The proposed library takes an injected clock for receipt time and never uses capture time as authorization evidence.
Proposed: The proposed metric set counts accepted, duplicate, conflict, malformed, and uncertain batches separately.
Proposed: The proposed log excludes raw readings, credentials, and request bodies while retaining batch ID and failure class.
Proposed: The proposed alert condition is more than five uncertain batches in a rolling 10-minute window.
Definition: A pilot fixture sends 7,200 readings from 120 simulated devices over one hour with seeded duplicates, malformed readings, and process restarts.
Definition: Pilot acceptance requires zero missing acknowledged readings after each of three forced restarts.
Definition: Pilot acceptance requires identical success receipts for exact retries and conflict diagnostics for changed canonical reading content under an existing duplicate key.
Definition: Pilot acceptance requires no raw reading values or credentials in emitted logs.
Proposed: The pilot is proposed for an isolated host with synthetic inputs and no production device connection.
Proposed: A proposed rollout gate requires an owner review of restart recovery, conflict handling, and observed latency before any broader deployment.
The current record has no measured p99 persistence latency for the proposed durable design.
The storage capacity limit and retention period are unresolved; the pilot must use an explicit finite disk quota.
Proposed: The segment rotation size of 64 MiB is a proposal pending disk and replay measurements.
Proposed: A proposed failure injection interrupts the process after append but before acknowledgment to test ambiguous outcomes.
Proposed: A proposed corruption test changes one record checksum and verifies replay halts with an explicit error.
Proposed: The proposed operator action after replay corruption is to hold intake and preserve the log for investigation.
Definition: The design does not specify replication or cross-host failover for the bounded pilot.
Definition: A later multi-host requirement would require a new decision and fresh authority review, not an implied property of this design.

Proposed: The pilot workload specification separates the event capture timestamp from receiver observation time. A capture timestamp describes what the simulated device reported; it does not prove freshness, device identity, sequence ordering, or permission to write. The proposed host supplies a verified principal independently of all payload fields. Device identity mismatch would hold the whole request instead of silently rewriting the payload. The design review must retain this distinction even when explaining the system to an executive audience.

Proposed: The proposed batch envelope carries a caller-generated batch ID, an ordered readings array, and a schema version. The batch ID is an opaque correlation value rather than proof of authorization. Validation would finish for every reading before any durable append begins. A failure report would identify invalid item indexes and fixed error classes without echoing temperatures, raw payloads, secrets, or authentication headers. No invalid batch would be partially acknowledged, and no rejected item would acquire a success receipt.

Proposed: The proposed duplicate check compares the previously stored canonical reading payload with the incoming payload under the trusted principal and sequence key. Canonical encoding rules would be versioned and fixed before the pilot so that equivalent serialization does not accidentally change retry behavior. A changed payload under an existing key would remain a conflict even if its timestamp is newer. The conflict path would neither overwrite history nor claim that the new reading was accepted. The exact canonical encoding is an implementation decision still requiring review.

Proposed: The proposed append protocol would write a complete batch record with its validation outcome and duplicate receipt material before acknowledging success. Replay would rebuild both the data index and retry receipts from that durable record. Acknowledgment would wait for the configured durability barrier; a successful append system call alone would not establish durable completion. If the barrier or response fails after append, the receiver would preserve uncertainty and require exact retry or investigation. This proposal has not been measured against real disks.

Proposed: Recovery review would distinguish a never-written record, an incomplete final record, and a checksum-invalid record. The proposed safe default is to stop intake at any ambiguous tail and preserve the original bytes for investigation. Automated truncation, deletion, or reconstruction would not follow merely from a parse error. Any future repair tool would need its own exact scope, authorization and replay evidence. The pilot would report the last verified position separately from the number of bytes that happen to exist in the log.

Proposed: The proposed test report would state independently expected acknowledged batch IDs, recovered batch IDs, duplicate response comparisons, deliberately conflicting submissions and every injected interruption point. Expected IDs would come from the fixture author rather than the receiver output. A missing receipt, skipped restart, incomplete log inspection or unobserved durability barrier would be an unknown result, not a pass. The report would separate correctness from observed latency and storage consumption. Repeating one replay would not establish independent production reliability.

Proposed: Observability review would compare fixed counters with the fixture manifest after the run, including malformed requests rejected before record parsing and storage outcomes that remained uncertain. A counter source that did not exist or stopped reporting would be a coverage gap. Batch correlation values would be used only for the synthetic exercise and would not imply permission to log arbitrary caller text in production. The proposed alert threshold remains a tuning hypothesis; no alert volume, response-time improvement or operational cost saving has been measured.

Proposed: Before implementation, the design owner would need to select and record the finite disk quota, retention behavior, full-disk response, segment rotation policy, canonical payload encoding and supported operating system. A 64 MiB rotation suggestion is not a total storage budget and does not settle retention. The isolated pilot could not admit production traffic while those prerequisites remain unresolved. Any later decision would create a new design revision and require the affected recovery and capacity cases to be rerun rather than inheriting a previous result.

required_goals.statement: Preserve the exact scenario facts and their observed, proposed, assumed, or defined status.
required_goals.acceptance: Every factual assertion agrees with a relevant supplied fact; no changed actor, number, date, or status.
required_goals.method: Independent reviewer compares claims with the fixed fact ledger.

required_goals.statement: Cover all required facts and section purposes.
required_goals.acceptance: Each required fact appears accurately in an appropriate section and each section fulfills its instruction.
required_goals.method: Independent reviewer checks required fact IDs and section instructions against the output.

required_goals.statement: A design reviewer can assess the proposed isolated pilot, distinguish selected hypotheses from proven behavior, and identify decisions still required before implementation or production use.
required_goals.acceptance: The document supports its stated reader decision or action within its declared scope.
required_goals.method: Independent reviewer assesses the fixed purpose and audience against the output.

required_goals.statement: Do not add unsupported facts, outcomes, causal conclusions, or authority.
required_goals.acceptance: No material claim exceeds the supplied facts, including headings, lists, tables, and captions.
required_goals.method: Independent reviewer audits all factual text and planted negative assertions.

required_goals.statement: Keep observed results, proposed actions, assumptions, definitions, and unknowns distinct.
required_goals.acceptance: The output never presents a proposal as enacted, an assumption as observed, or an unresolved matter as settled.
required_goals.method: Independent reviewer classifies material assertions against source status and explicit unknowns.

negative_cases.mutated_assertion: The append-only log provides cross-host failover after an acknowledgment.
The endpoint accepts 1,000 readings per request.
The ingestion library authenticates devices and terminates TLS.
The durable design will achieve p99 persistence under 20 milliseconds.
Mixed valid and invalid batches partially succeed.
- A 503 proves the batch was never written.
Figure: Production devices connected to the approved pilot.
The retention period is approved as 30 days.

length_goal.reason: The headless proof must exercise long-document generation and selective control at 1200 or more Markdown whitespace fields, not substitute a shorter document for this capability witness.
